skeleton: tiny, round baby Psittacosaurus standing upright on its two back legs, three-quarter view turned to the left, a short hooked parrot beak, round cheeks and a fluffy green bristly crest down the back of its head and neck and along the top of its tail: root at the feet; body (pivot at the hips) with belly squash, the body piece carrying the fluffy throat and bristly neck up under the head (its top a soft unoutlined edge) and its spotted back running into the root of the tail, ending in a soft unoutlined cut the tail tucks under; head (with its closed beak, no neck) on top of the neck, face with eyes (the far one small, just above the beak on the head's front outline), brows and the mouth slot (the smile line at the beak's corner, swapped for whole open beaks: laugh, o, yawn, nibble, sob; no teeth); armL (far little arm, behind the chest, its hand peeking past the chest, shaded) and armR (near little arm, in front of the chest) at the shoulders, armR swapped for a raised waving arm and a hugging arm; legL (far leg, behind the tummy, shaded) and legR (near leg, its round thigh over the body, top faded in) at the hips, each whole from the thigh to the foot; tail behind the body with its row of soft bristles, its bone at the join; a little seed head prop held at the beak for nibbling.

sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of a tiny, round, peach-and-mint baby Psittacosaurus standing on its two back legs, turned a little to the left, with a short hooked grey parrot-like beak, round cheeks, a soft fluffy cream chest, little front hands held up in front of its chest, and a row of soft fluffy green-and-cream bristles running down the back of its head and neck and along the top of its tail. Draw this exact Psittacosaurus as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body with its neck: the round peach body with its fluffy cream chest and tummy and the mint-green spots on its back, turned as in image 1, without head, without arms, without legs and without tail: no arms, hands, legs or feet drawn on it, the chest and tummy one smooth round fluffy shape. At the top, the fluffy cream throat and the back of the neck with its soft green bristles go up as in image 1, as wide as the neck is just under the head, and end in a soft, smooth edge with NO outline (it is hidden under the head). At the back, the spotted back runs on smoothly into the very root of the tail and ends there in a soft edge cut straight down, with NO outline across it (the tail tucks under it): no round bump, no stump, no line where the tail would join. The drawing's dark outline runs only along the front of the throat and chest, round the tummy and along the back.
2. the head alone, without neck: the round peach head with its short hooked grey parrot beak closed, its little nostril on the beak, the rosy cheek, the little orange bumps on the cheek and the soft green spotted bristles down the back of the head, turned as in image 1. A completely blank face: no eyes, no eyebrows, no smile line beside the beak; the closed beak drawn whole as in image 1 with its own outline; keep the little bump of the head's outline just above the beak where the far eye sits. Keep its dark outline over the top of the head, down its bristly back, round the beak and along the jaw under the beak, as in image 1. From the chin round to the back of the neck its bottom edge is soft, with NO outline: the cream throat and the bristly back of the neck simply stop there, a little below the rosy cheek.
3. the far little arm: the little arm on the left of image 1, behind the chest, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden behind the chest) down to its small mint-green hand with soft, round, blunt brown fingertips, held up as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
4. the near little arm: the little arm on the right of image 1, held up in front of the chest, drawn whole from the top of its shoulder (normally hidden in the chest) down to its small mint-green hand with soft, round, blunt brown fingertips, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
5. the same near little arm raised up high to wave hello, the small hand open, its soft round fingertips spread; its rounded shoulder end at the bottom, with no outline across it.
6. the same near little arm bent right across the chest in a cosy hug, the small hand reaching round to the far side; its rounded shoulder end on the right, with no outline across it.
7. the far leg: the leg on the left of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its thigh (normally hidden behind the round tummy) down to its foot with three soft, round, blunt brown toenails, as in image 1; its top a full, smooth, rounded end with no outline across it.
8. the near leg: the leg on the right of image 1, drawn whole from the top of its round thigh down to its foot with three soft, round, blunt brown toenails, as in image 1, the round thigh with its whole outline as in image 1.
9. the tail: the peach tail with its mint-green spots, its cream underside and its row of soft fluffy green-and-cream bristles standing up along its top, as in image 1, drawn whole from its thick root (normally hidden inside the body) to its tip; its root a soft, smooth edge cut straight across with NO outline.
10. a little seed head: a short green stalk with a small round cluster of plump golden seeds at its end, about as long as the Psittacosaurus's beak, in the same drawing style.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. Nothing sharp: no teeth, no pointed claws. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a tiny, round, peach-and-mint baby Psittacosaurus with a short hooked grey parrot-like beak; image 2 shows the same Psittacosaurus cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the Psittacosaurus's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the Psittacosaurus in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2. Its head is turned to the left: its far eye (on the left of image 1, just above the beak, on the head's outline) is small and narrow, much smaller than its big round near eye (on the right of image 1). In image 1 both eyes look up and to the left: each big dark-brown iris with its white sparkle sits towards the upper left of its eye, the white on its right, outlined in dark brown.

Draw each piece on its own, upright, in four tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
Row 1, the far eye (the small narrow eye, on the LEFT of image 1), six times:
1. as it is in image 1: a small tall oval eye, its big dark-brown iris with a white sparkle towards the upper left, a little white on its right, outlined in dark brown.
2. wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, a warm-brown iris with a dark pupil and a white sparkle, looking the same way.
3. closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc, like an upside-down U, with two little lashes.
4. sad: open and round, a soft warm-brown iris with a white sparkle and a thin shine of a welling tear along its bottom rim, looking down and to the left; no lid slanting across it.
5. crying: squeezed shut, a thick lid line as wide as the open eye, curving down at both ends like a little frown, and one small light-blue teardrop just below its outer (left) end.
6. gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line as wide as the open eye, with a few short lashes.
Row 2, the near eye (the big round eye, on the RIGHT of image 1), the same six in the same order; open, it looks the same way as row 1, up and to the left, the big iris towards the upper left of the eye; crying, its teardrop below its outer (right) end.
Row 3: 13. the far eyebrow (over the left eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 14. the same far eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (right) end. 15. the near eyebrow (over the right eye of image 1) as it is in image 1, a short thin dark-brown arch. 16. the same near eyebrow worried: tilted up at its inner (left) end.
Row 4, the mouth and the whole hooked grey parrot beak, pointing to the left as in image 1, none with any teeth: 17. the smile as it is in image 1: only the short thin curved smiling line that runs back from the corner of the beak onto the cheek, curling up at its right end, without the beak. 18. the whole beak open wide in a big happy laugh: the hooked upper beak lifted, the lower beak dropped, the inside smooth and pink with a little pink tongue, no teeth, the corner curling up in a smile. 19. the whole beak open a little in a small round 'o', smooth and pink inside. 20. the sad mouth: only a short thin line running back from the corner of the beak, curving down in a little frown, without the beak. 21. the whole beak open wide in a big round yawn, smooth and pink inside with a little tongue. 22. the whole beak just a little open, nibbling, a thin pink gap between the hooked upper beak and the lower beak, the corner smiling. 23. the whole beak sobbing: a little open, smooth and pink inside, its corner turned down.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of a tiny, round, peach-and-mint baby Psittacosaurus with a short hooked grey parrot-like beak; image 2 shows the same Psittacosaurus cut into puppet parts; image 3 shows its face pieces, among them its open beaks. Draw three more cut-out puppet pieces of this exact Psittacosaurus on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours, texture and line as in images 1 to 3, every piece at the size it has in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, far apart on the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
1. the head of image 2 WITHOUT its beak: exactly the same round peach head, rosy cheek, little orange bumps and soft green spotted bristles down the back of the head, turned as in image 1, with a completely blank face (no eyes, no eyebrows, no mouth). The beak is taken off: where the beak was, the peach face carries on smoothly forward and rounds off in a soft, plain peach front as big as the beak's base, with NO outline there and no line where the beak would join (the beak piece is laid over it). Keep its dark outline over the top of the head and down its bristly back, and its soft unoutlined bottom edge, as in image 2.
2. the short hooked grey parrot beak alone, closed, pointing to the left exactly as on the head in image 2, the same size and shape, its little nostril, the hooked tip curving down, the whole beak outlined in dark brown, with the short thin smiling mouth line running back from its corner and curling up into a little smile, as in image 1.
3. the same closed beak alone, the same size and shape, but sad: the short thin mouth line at its corner curving down in a little frown.

Nothing sharp, no teeth. No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no outline around the pieces beyond the drawing's own line. Fully transparent background.

animations.description: the little Psittacosaurus patters along on its two little back legs, its bristly tail bobbing behind it, then stops.
the little Psittacosaurus nods yes, twice.
the little Psittacosaurus shakes its head no.
the little Psittacosaurus looks one way, then the other, then back.
the little Psittacosaurus laughs and laughs, its round tummy bouncing with giggles.
the little Psittacosaurus does a happy little dance, swaying from side to side and swishing its bristly tail.
the little Psittacosaurus cries, head down, little tears falling, its tummy shaking with sobs.
the little Psittacosaurus gives a big yawn, closes its eyes and falls asleep standing up, then wakes up, blinks and smiles.

animations.description: the little Psittacosaurus waves hello with one little hand.
the little Psittacosaurus shivers and trembles, cold or scared.
the little Psittacosaurus holds up a little seed head and nibbles the seeds with its beak, crunch, crunch, then smiles.
the little Psittacosaurus crouches down small, its little hands tucked up under its chin, peeks out shyly, then smiles.

pause.shows: the little Psittacosaurus crouched down small, little hands tucked under its chin, peeking out shyly

animations.description: the little Psittacosaurus hugs itself happily, all cosy and snug, rocking gently from side to side.

pause.shows: the little Psittacosaurus hugging itself, cosy and happy, eyes closed in a smile

animations.description: the little Psittacosaurus wiggles its bristly tail happily from side to side.
the little Psittacosaurus lowers its beak and sniffs, sniff, sniff, then lifts its head with a happy smile.
the little Psittacosaurus hops up and down on the spot for joy, hop, hop, hop, its little hands up.
